relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-code read of attacker-controlled fuzzer input. pixDeserializeFromMemory parses the SPIX-format byte stream into width, height, depth, and ncolors, then materializes a PIX object. The PIX flows into the harness as pixs and is processed through pixThresholdTo4bpp, pixColorGray, and cleanup, where the UAF occurs.

Destroys pix1 and its colormap via pixFree -> pixDestroyColormap -> pixcmapDestroy. The fuzzer's local cmap variable, obtained earlier via pixGetColormap(pix1), still holds a pointer to the now-freed PIXCMAP. No mechanism nullifies external aliases. The fix removes the redundant pixcmapDestroy(&cmap) call at line 48 since pixDestroy already handles colormap cleanup through ownership.

Reads cmap->array (8 bytes) from the freed PIXCMAP struct. Called from colorquant_fuzzer.cc:48 via pixcmapDestroy(&cmap) with a dangling pointer. The PIXCMAP was already freed by pixDestroy(&pix1) through pixFree -> pixDestroyColormap -> pixcmapDestroy at colormap.c:292-293.
cmap = pixGetColormap(pix1) returns pix1->colormap, a non-owning raw pointer alias to the PIXCMAP owned by pix1.
Intermediate runtime event cleanup_obligation materialized from verified transition assertion A4.

edges.description: The cmap pointer alias obtained at line 22 persists unchanged to line 37 where pixDestroy(&pix1) frees the PIXCMAP through the ownership chain. No code path between lines 22 and 37 modifies or nullifies cmap.

After pixDestroy(&pix1) frees the PIXCMAP, the same cmap pointer value (now dangling) propagates to the cleanup section. In the vulnerable version, the redundant pixcmapDestroy(&cmap) call at line 48 dereferences this dangling pointer, causing the UAF.
